name: Question 5
problem:
Find the equation of the tangent line to the polar curve $r={e}^{-\theta }$ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4},$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta )={e}^{-\theta }(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=-{e}^{-\theta }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta )={e}^{-\theta }(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=-{e}^{-\theta }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-\theta }(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}{{e}^{-\theta }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )} \\  & =-\frac{\cancel{{e}^{-\theta }}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}{\cancel{{e}^{-\theta }}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4} \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\pi /4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4}).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4} & =0\cdot (x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4}) \\ y-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4} & =0 \\ y & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}{e}^{-\pi /4}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point P, we follow four steps:

Step 1: Calculate the derivative dydx:

In this case, we're given that

y′(θ)=e−θ(−sin⁡θ+cos⁡θ),x′(θ)=−e−θ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ).

Therefore, we can find dydx as follows:

dydx=y′(θ)x′(θ)=−e−θ(−sin⁡θ+cos⁡θ)e−θ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)=−e−θ(−sin⁡θ+cos⁡θ)e−θ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)=sin⁡θ−cos⁡θcos⁡θ+sin⁡θ

Step 2: Find the slope of the tangent at P:

The slope of the tangent line is

m=dydx|θ=π/4=(sin⁡(π4)−cos⁡(π4))(cos⁡(π4)+sin⁡(π4))=(22−22)(22+22)=02=0.

Step 3: Find the Cartesian coordinates of P:

We compute the xy-coordinates of P as follows:

x1=rcos⁡θ=e−θcos⁡θ=e−π/4cos⁡(π4)=22e−π/4y1=rsin⁡θ=e−θsin⁡θ=e−π/4sin⁡(π4)=22e−π/4

Therefore, the coordinates of P are (22e−π/4,22e−π/4).

Step 4: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

y−y1=m(x−x1)y−22e−π/4=0⋅(x−22e−π/4)y−22e−π/4=0y=22e−π/4
